conviction_note: Lean long, about 56% up: the one product line (YARTEMLEA) went from 30 to 73 ordering accounts by 30 Jun, got a permanent J-code on 1 Jul, lost its only late-stage adult competitor on 27 Jul, and the company said on 16 Oct it was ending EU compassionate use because of 'increasing demand for YARTEMLEA drug supply in the U.S. commercial market'. About 17% of float is short (7.8 days to cover). The lean is capped because the revenue bar is disputed ($30.9M at Earnings Whispers, $35.5M at Benzinga, $38.0M at Chartmill) and the 25-delta skew pays for downside (+10.65 vol points). abs_move_pct stays at the 16% option-implied move. The findings sum to +6.0 against a scaled +1.9; the gap is the disputed bar, carried in p_up and not taken off the findings.
bar: Q3 2026 net revenue. Earnings Whispers consensus is $30.9M, about +8% on Q2's $28.5M, with EPS of -$0.05 (https://finviz.com/news/421146/omeros-faces-its-first-real-test-of-whether-the-yartemlia-launch-can-keep-climbing, 2026-11-11). Other aggregators disagree: Benzinga $35.5M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OMER/earnings-forecasts) and Chartmill $38.0M with EPS +$0.03 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/OMER/estimates); Tickeron's $17-19M looks stale. There is no company revenue guide. Because the bar has no company guide and no two agreeing sources, every revenue-line finding is capped small (lesson 6). print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of about $33M net against the $30.9M Earnings Whispers figure; against $35.5M it would be about -7%.
positioning_check: About 12.83M shares short with 7.8 days to cover, shown on shortsqueeze.com on 2026-11-16 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=OMER), against 11.43M and 6.7 days on the same site's page dated 2026-10-29, so short interest is rising. A search snippet from a tracker (https://equibles.com/stocks/omer/shortinterest) gives 12.5M, 17.3% of float and 9.3 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement. Using the roughly 73M shares implied by Q2 EPS, that is about 17% short: a crowded short. Options: 25-delta skew is +10.65 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest is 0.25 (call-heavy), the ATM spread is 72% of mid so the 16.05% event-implied move is indicative only, and ATM IV is 180%. The skew and the crowded short point opposite ways; I lean long because a crowded short against an account-driven launch ramp is a squeeze mechanism, and I size small because of the skew.

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, net revenue needs to clearly clear about $32-35M with ordering accounts well above 73, management needs to describe reorders or growing use per account rather than a one-time stocking of new centres, and the call needs a constructive read on the NTAP that started 1 October.

next_guide.company_current_guide: No YARTEMLEA revenue guidance ('we are not providing revenue guidance at this time'). Q3 operating expenses guided 'slightly higher' than Q2, interest expense about $6.5M, company-wide cash-flow positive by mid-2027 (Q2 call, 2026-08-12, https://www.webull.com/news/15432272178070528).
next_guide.basis: Management has declined revenue guidance on both 2026 calls until it has more experience with prescribing trends. The new information for Q4 commentary is the NTAP of up to $287k per Medicare inpatient course, effective 2026-10-01, which the call may describe qualitatively. A first revenue guide is possible but nothing sourced points to one.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue ramp rests on the Q2 account build. Ordering accounts rose from 30 (31 Mar) to 73 (30 Jun), out of about 175 transplant centres. Management said ordering frequency rose in Q2, distributor inventory held at about 1.5 weeks so there was no stocking, the permanent J-code took effect 1 Jul, and adults were about 75% of Q2 sales. Q3 is the first quarter with all 73+ accounts ordering. Against the $30.9M Earnings Whispers bar (+8% on $28.5M), the account base alone points to a beat; against the $35.5-38.0M figures elsewhere it is about at the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On YARTEMLEA revenue: Q2 net $28.5M against about $12.5M bought +26.55%; Q1 net $9.9M (first launch quarter) sold -7.65%. Median absolute reaction over the last 8 prints is 11.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is split: one aggregator asks only +8% QoQ while two others sit at $35.5-38M, so the market has no shared number. If the ramp were priced the stock would sit near its post-Q2 high of $21.24 and not at $17.23 with 17% of float short and puts bid. The CHMP drop in October took the stock down for a reason unrelated to US revenue.
findings.independence: Q2 call (account frequency up, inventory at 1.5 weeks): https://www.webull.com/news/15432272178070528. The mid-quarter demand statement is a separate document (next finding).

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement, 2026-10-16: Omeros told the CHMP it will end the EU YARTEMLEA compassionate-use programme 'due to increasing demand for YARTEMLEA drug supply in the U.S. commercial market'; current patients finish their courses. This is the only company statement on US demand made after the Q2 call (12 Aug) and before this print, and it came after the Q3 quarter closed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance. The 16 Oct release as a whole drew -14 to -15% on the CHMP outcome, so the demand sentence was buried under the regulatory headline.
findings.why_not_priced: It sat in a release the market read as negative (the stock fell about 15% that day), and no preview I found cites it. If it had been read as a demand signal, Q3 previews would quote it and the bar would not include a $30.9M figure that implies a near-stall.
findings.independence: Same release reported by stocktwits (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/Markets/Equity/omeros-shares-slide-after-chmp-upholds-negative-opinion-on-drug-analyst-sees-buying-opportunity-at-16/cZxKQ9ERBtG); the regulatory finding below rests on the same document. The statement is qualitative, a company claim with no number in it.

findings.finding: Expectations: about 17% of float is short (12.83M shares, 7.8 days to cover on 2026-11-16, up from 11.43M on 2026-10-29). The stock is 18% below its 52-week high and about half the $33 H.C. Wainwright target. Earnings Whispers says the street is 'not asking for another explosion'. Put/call open interest is 0.25, but the 25-delta skew is +10.65 (downside paid).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: With heavy short interest in August, the Q2 beat produced +26.55%. Q1 (30 accounts, $9.9M) produced -7.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: A crowded short is the market's bet against the ramp continuing. If the bet had been abandoned, short interest would be falling into the print rather than rising, and the stock would not be near its post-CHMP level.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/421146/omeros-faces-its-first-real-test-of-whether-the-yartemlia-launch-can-keep-climbing). The skew in the baseline points the other way.

findings.finding: Next guide: NTAP of up to $287k per Medicare inpatient course took effect 2026-10-01, after the permanent J-code on 1 Jul. This is the first quarter the call can describe hospital uptake under NTAP. The company gives no revenue guidance, guided Q3 opex slightly higher, and targets company-wide positive cash flow by mid-2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no revenue guide yet. Q2's qualitative 'strong momentum' commentary came with the +26.55% move.
findings.why_not_priced: The NTAP is public, but its effect on Q4 ordering is not; no preview quantifies it, and Earnings Whispers says it 'should appear in the outlook rather than reported Q3 numbers'.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the NTAP grant (https://s21.q4cdn.com/975996899/files/doc_news/Omeros-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-2026.pdf); Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11.

findings.finding: Up to $100M of 'near-term' Novo Nordisk milestones on zaltenibart are still unpaid, out of $340M upfront plus near-term ($240M received at the 25 Nov 2025 close). The triggers are undisclosed, management called its confidence 'high', and the Q2 release said the Novo programme was 'on track toward Phase 3 trial initiation'. If a milestone was triggered in Q3 or Q4 it would likely appear in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement in Oct 2025 and the Q4 2025 print (+25.32% on 2025-11-13) are the comparable events; no milestone receipt has been reported yet.
findings.why_not_priced: Because the trigger is undisclosed, the market cannot date the payment. $100M is about 8% of a roughly $1.26B market cap, so a confirmed receipt would be visible.
findings.independence: The Q2 release's 'on track toward Phase 3 trial initiation' (https://s21.q4cdn.com/975996899/files/doc_news/Omeros-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-2026.pdf). I found no first-patient-dosed news, which argues for the low end.

findings.finding: Competitor: AstraZeneca/Alexion's Ultomiris adult/adolescent TA-TMA Phase 3 (TMA-313) missed its primary endpoint on 2026-07-27, inside Q3, leaving YARTEMLEA as the only approved therapy for adults (about 75% of its sales). The paediatric study read out positively and Alexion is filing in paediatric HSCT-TMA, which threatens the roughly 25% paediatric share later.
findings.link: Same indication (HSCT-associated TMA) and the same prescribers; off-label C5 inhibition is what YARTEMLEA displaces, and Q2 commentary cited responses in patients who had failed off-label C5. Adults are about 75% of YARTEMLEA sales.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed separately; it came 16 days before the Q2 print, which rose +26.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public since July. What is not yet seen is the effect on Q3 adult share, which this print shows for the first time.

findings.finding: Insider sales after Q2: director Arnold Hanish exercised and sold 15,000 shares at $18.53-19.02 on 2026-08-26/27 with no 10b5-1 flag; CAO David Borges sold 20,000 at $20.95 on 2026-09-22/23 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-02-10. Both are small (about $0.7M combined).
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public, but the sales are small option exercise-and-sell trades; nobody previews them.
findings.independence: CAO Form 4 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1285819/000143774926031169/rdgdoc.xml (2026-09-24, 10b5-1, so weak as a signal).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-28, 19 days before the print, the board granted the CEO 500,000 performance options struck at $17.88 (market) with 30-day VWAP hurdles of $25/$30/$35/$40 (8-K filed 2026-10-30).
findings.why_not_priced: A comp 8-K draws no coverage. A board striking options at market just before a print it has already seen the internal numbers for is a weak tell that it did not expect a collapse.

findings.finding: CHMP re-examination upheld the negative opinion on narsoplimab in TA-TMA on 2026-10-16. Omeros says the expert group never received the patient-level data it submitted in August; it would license EU rights to a third party if approval comes. The call may set out the EU path (a new MAA or litigation) and the change in compassionate-use cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: June CHMP negative: steep drop (stocktwits calls 16 Oct the steepest since late June); 16 Oct re-exam: about -14 to -15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced already. H.C. Wainwright had taken Europe out of its model in June. Only a residual from the call's EU commentary is left.
findings.independence: This shares the 16 Oct announcement with the mid-quarter demand finding; finviz/InvestorsHub covers the same release.

findings.finding: Likely GAAP noise: Q1 and Q2 carried $73.1M and $11.5M of non-cash GAAP gains from marking the 2029 convertible note derivative to market. The stock traded $15.85-21.24 after Q2 against $6.70-14.72 the quarter before, so Q3 probably carries a non-cash loss on the remaining $40.3M of notes, which could make headline GAAP EPS look weak against the -$0.05 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1's large GAAP gain did not prevent a -7.65% reaction; the market read revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from the price path and the derivative's sign; previews do not mention it. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Price range from Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11 (finviz URL above). This is an inference, not a disclosed figure.

outside_window.finding: Alexion is filing Ultomiris in paediatric HSCT-TMA after a positive single-arm study; a paediatric approval would compete for about 25% of YARTEMLEA sales.

Two investigator-sponsored YARTEMLEA studies (hyperinflammatory ARDS, prophylactic paediatric TA-TMA) are expected to begin enrolling by year-end 2026; the OMS527 inpatient trial is also expected to start by year-end.

baseline_tension: Cuts against the skew (+10.65, downside paid) and with the crowded short, which is the squeeze mechanism; the 20-day run-up of +5.4% is a partial recovery from the -15% CHMP day, not a run into the print. p_up is held at 56 rather than higher for that reason and for the disputed bar.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): consensus ranges from $30.9M to $38.0M with no company guide, so the revenue finding was cut from +3.0 to +2.0 and the demand statement from +2.0 to +1.5; print_vs_bar cut from +10 to +6; p_up from 57 to 56.
Lesson 7 (sign against skew): kept long with an explicit reason (17% short with rising short interest, call-heavy open interest); no further cut, because lesson 6 already moved p_up.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): derivative mark-to-market loss resized from -0.5 to -0.3, a fraction, since it has no path to the guide.
Novo milestone cut from +1.0 to +0.7: no document dates the trigger (lesson 5, an inference sized small).
Lesson 1 left the reaction sizes standing: this name has paid for revenue beats (+26.55% on Q2).
